content:
Lenovo has launched a colourful new laptop, the IdeaPad Vibe, taking aim at the MacBook Neo.

Lenovo unveiled the IdeaPad Vibe at its Lenovo Innovation World event on the eve of IFA, clearly setting its sights on Apple's most accessible and beloved MacBook Neo. Based on the specs, this laptop is absolutely up for the fight. Users can choose between 14-inch and 15-inch OLED displays; the chassis measures 14.9mm thick and starts at 2.87 pounds. Although it's thicker and larger than Apple's laptop, at least the starting weight isn't significantly heavier. Lenovo says the Vibe will be available in plastic and metal chassis options.

But the design is genuinely eye-catching — Lenovo has partnered with Pantone to release the IdeaPad Vibe in seven different colours, including:

Dreamy Purple: A soft purple tone with enchanting layers, radiating a calming energy that makes you feel at ease wherever you go. Spicy Gold: A rich golden tone blending warmth and energy, giving off a confident and approachable feel. Zen Green: A nature-inspired green that exudes balance and harmony, inviting you to slow down. Icy Blue: A minimalist cool-toned blue that brings refreshing clarity and a sense of renewal. Lively Coral: A warm, uplifting colour with a touch of optimistic orange, spreading friendly positive energy wherever it goes. Mystery Blue: A deep blue tone radiating trust, confidence and elegance. Steadfast Grey: A classic grey that exudes strength, poise and understated taste.

The keyboard also features swappable keycaps, allowing users to freely mix and match different colour combinations to suit their personal style.

But good looks are just the basics — Lenovo has equipped this laptop with a rather attractive array of ports: two USB-A ports, one HDMI port, two USB-C ports, a headphone jack, and even a microSD card reader. There's also a 5-megapixel camera (with a physical privacy shutter), an optional keyboard backlight, and an optional touchscreen exclusive to the 15-inch model.

So what about the internal specs?

Users can choose between AMD Ryzen AI 400 chips or Qualcomm Snapdragon X chips. The AMD model supports up to 32GB of RAM and is user-upgradeable. Storage goes up to 1TB, also upgradeable, with dual slots. The Snapdragon version supports up to 24GB of RAM; storage remains upgradeable, but RAM does not. Lenovo says an Intel version will arrive later.

The Lenovo IdeaPad Vibe will go on sale in two phases. The AMD model will launch in October, followed by the Snapdragon model in November. Both start at $699.99 — a price point that, now that Apple has raised RAM pricing, matches the MacBook Neo.

Meanwhile, Lenovo also unveiled the IdeaCentre AIO I all-in-one desktop, available with 24-inch or 27-inch displays, colour options similar to the Vibe, starting at $939. The product will also begin shipping in November.
